4579.title: [Apple] Backport 26.0 library and unversioned app TFMs
4579.body:
[Apple] Backport 26.0 library and unversioned app TFMs (#4579)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/4031
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/3798

SkiaSharp 3.119.4 packages inherited Apple target platform versions of
26.2 from the .NET 10 upgrade. This prevents Mac Catalyst native assets
from resolving for Avalonia applications targeting 26.0 and causes Uno
iOS builds on older 26.x workloads to select platform-neutral assemblies,
leading to registrar and linker failures.

Backport the fix already shipped in v4: pin Apple library packages to the
base 26.0 TPV while leaving app and test TFMs unversioned so they use the
installed workload. Align the reference-pack metadata and update the
Android, iOS, and Mac Catalyst test tasks to their unversioned TFMs,
avoiding mismatched output paths and NETSDK1005 restore failures.

Co-authored-by: Tim Miller <898335+drasticactions@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <mattleibow@live.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

4105.title: Fix x86 .NET Framework threading test OOM failures
4105.body:
Fix x86 .NET Framework threading test OOM failures (#4105)

Backport of #3674 to release/3.119.x.
Fixes #3608

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/3674
Fixes: chronically-red "Windows (.NET Framework)" (net48/x86) Tests job on release/3.119.x

The internal Tests pipeline on release/3.119.x has been red for months.
The failing job is Windows (.NET Framework) on x86, where
SKBitmapThreadingTest.ImageScalingMultipleThreadsTest(100, 1000) and
SKObjectTest.EnsureMultithreadingDoesNotThrow(1000) throw "Unable to
allocate pixels for the bitmap", with adjacent tests dying as collateral
in the same starved process.

These tests intentionally create native SkiaSharp objects without
disposing them so they are reclaimed only by the GC and finalizer thread
— that is the point of the tests: they verify SkiaSharp objects can be
finalized safely from many threads concurrently. Disposing would defeat
the purpose (an earlier "add using" attempt was wrong and was reverted).
The real cause is an environment limit: on x86 (.NET Framework, 2 GB
address space) the heaviest variants queue more undisposed native
allocations than the finalizer can keep pace with, so Skia's allocator
fails. The 64-bit .NET Core jobs have enough address space and pass.

  * Skip the known-OOM combinations on x86 only (IntPtr.Size == 4) — a
    sanctioned environment skip, not masking a product bug.
  * Add lighter intermediate variants (10x100 and 100) so concurrent
    GC/finalizer behavior is still exercised on x86 at lower load.
  * Document the test purpose and that disposal is intentionally omitted,
    so future readers don't "fix" it by adding using.

Touches tests only:
tests/SkiaSharp.Tests.Console/SkiaSharp/SKBitmapThreadingTest.cs and
tests/Tests/SkiaSharp/SKObjectTest.cs (+28/-0).

Validated by a full pipeline run that built natives fresh in-run
(3.119.5-preview.0.3+merge): all stages succeeded, including every
Tests-stage job. The previously chronically-red net48/x86 job now passes.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
4105.author: mattleibow

4086.title: Fix WinUI Projection DLL not found for .NET 9 consumers
4086.body:
[3.119.x] Fix WinUI Projection DLL not resolved for .NET 9 consumers on Windows (#4086)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/4082
Cherry-pick of: #4084

Backport of the same fix to the 3.119.x release branch. The Projection DLL
was only placed in `runtimes/win-{arch}/lib/net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0/`,
which NuGet won't serve to net9 consumers. .NET 9 apps hit a
`FileNotFoundException` for `SkiaSharp.Views.WinUI.Native.Projection` at
startup.

Include the Projection DLL in both the `$(WindowsTargetFrameworksCurrent)`
(net10.0) and `$(WindowsTargetFrameworksPrevious)` (net9.0) runtime folders
so NuGet resolves it for both .NET 9 and .NET 10 consumers.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <mattleibow@live.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

4045.title: [release/3.119.x] Fix CI failures: ANGLE, WASM 2.0.6, Tizen SDK, Alpine
4045.body:
[CI] Fix native build failures on release/3.119.x (#4045)

Context: #4014, #4022, #3743, #4013

Four independent CI failures were blocking all builds on the 3.119.x
release branch. Each fix is backported from main and adapted to the
older file layout (scripts/ vs scripts/infra/).

~~ ANGLE WinAppSDK download (WinError 10013) ~~

DevDiv 1ES agents block Python's urllib from making outbound HTTPS
connections. Replace the winappsdk_setup.py invocation with a Cake
DownloadFile() from dnceng's dotnet-public feed, followed by a new
PowerShell script (generate_winappsdk_headers.ps1) that runs winmdidl
+ midlrt to produce the C++ headers ANGLE needs.

~~ WASM Emscripten 2.0.6 hang ~~

The 2.0.6 build intermittently hangs in CI. No .NET release ever
consumed this version — it was a legacy artifact from early
experimentation. Remove it from the matrix and merge lists.

~~ Tizen SDK 6.1 permanently broken ~~

Samsung rebranded Tizen Studio to Tizen SDK starting with version 10.0
and the old 6.1 Certificate-Manager package fails deterministically
with NoClassDefFoundError. Update to SDK 10.0 with the new URL pattern.

~~ Alpine apk.static transient download failures ~~

GitLab returns intermittent HTTP 5xx for apk.static. Without --fail,
curl silently saves the error body and the script tries to chmod +x a
JSON string. Add --fail --retry 5 --retry-delay 10 --retry-all-errors.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
